name: Ron M. Vachris

career.title: Forklift driver (seasonal job), then assistant warehouse manager in Phoenix
Warehouse manager in Colorado and Arizona, through the 1993 Price Club-Costco merger
Regional Vice President, San Diego (Southern California warehouses)
Senior Vice President and General Manager (Western region), then SVP of Real Estate Development
Executive Vice President, Chief Operating Officer of Merchandising

background_rationale: Spent more than 40 years inside Price Club and Costco, starting as a forklift driver and serving in warehouse operations, regional management, real estate and merchandising before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: In a Fortune interview, Vachris said it had been ingrained in him for 41 years that culture is not a priority but "the priority" at Costco.
Costco raised U.S. and Canadian membership fees for the first time since 2017, lifting Gold Star and Business memberships from $60 to $65 and Executive memberships from $120 to $130.

Costco sued the U.S. government in the Court of International Trade seeking a full refund of tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act if the Supreme Court found them unlawful.
Costco announced its first mixed-use Costco Business Center, in Waipahu, Hawaii, following the opening of its first standalone gas station in Mission Viejo, California, in 2026.

personal_story.hook: Ron Vachris took a holiday-break forklift job at Price Club at 17 and never left; 42 years later he became CEO.
personal_story.summary: Vachris was born in 1965 on Staten Island to a Greek American family; his father, a utility lineman, moved the family to Arizona when Ron was a teenager. While studying business at Glendale Community College near Phoenix, he took a seasonal forklift job at Price Club over the 1982 holiday break and decided he was learning more about business on the warehouse floor than in class. He became an assistant warehouse manager, helped open Price Club's Colorado stores, and stayed on through the 1993 merger with Costco. He ran Southern California as a regional vice president for a decade, then moved into real estate alongside co-founder Jeff Brotman, which he called one of the best educations he had in global business, before leading merchandising and operations and becoming Costco's third CEO in January 2024.
